connections.why: Harvey's circulation made transfusion thinkable: blood put into one vein would go round the whole body.

Denis gave a madman calf's blood because its 'mildness and freshness' might allay the 'heat and ebullition' of his own: the first transfusions into people were reasoned as tempering blood's hot and cold qualities, the logic of the humors.
